_about: Physics lab targets. Real skateboarding scaled for a THUG-style cartoon game: gravity is 18 (not 9.8) on purpose, so airtimes and heights are tuned to what feels right, not to real physics. target = the feel we want, min_ok/max_ok = the band that still feels right.

ollie_height_tap.why: A real tap ollie clears about 0.2 to 0.5 m (Apunts 3D kinematics: board centre rises about 0.24 m); the world record full ollie is 1.14 m. THUG-style exaggeration: a tap pops about a metre so it clears a curb, bench or manual pad and reads on screen. The six levels' gaps are built on this pop: lowering it to 0.93 m (round-2 feel pass) failed Over The Funbox, Senior Steps, Lunch Roof and Neighbour's Fence in the bots, so the target follows the level design.

ollie_height_full.why: A real high ollie is 0.9 to 1.14 m (Guinness record, Aldrin Garcia 2011). THUG lets a full crouch clear a chest-high ledge with room to flip; at gravity 18 that is a pop of 8.5 m/s and about 2 m. The levels' biggest ollie gaps need it: a 1.72 m full ollie (ollie_max 7.9) dropped four levels' bots below 100.

ollie_airtime_tap.why: Skate-3 arc (round 7): the pop keeps its height (about 1 m) but the drop past the apex runs at tune.fall_gravity (1.35x) until the fall is ollie-fast, so a tap lands in about 0.63 s instead of hanging 0.68 s. Still fits one flip (0.42 s) with about 0.2 s to catch it. The old symmetric arc (0.683 s) fails the max.

ollie_airtime_full.why: Full ollie with the heavier fall (round 7): about 0.88 s, still room for a double flip (0.68 s) plus landing prep. The old symmetric arc (0.95 s) fails the max.

ollie_fall_rise_ratio.why: Full ollie: time from the apex to touchdown over the time from the pop to the apex. A symmetric parabola is 1.0 and reads floaty; Skate 3's ollie drops back faster than it rose. 1.35x gravity on the fall gives about 0.83 (0.40 s down, 0.48 s up).

push_time_to_top.why: Time from standing to 95% of push top speed. A real skater needs 3 to 5 pushes (about 4 s) to reach cruising speed. Games shorten that: under 1.5 s feels like a kart, over 4 s feels like a chore.

push_top_speed.why: A real skater cruises at 4 to 6 m/s by pushing. The game runs about twice as fast so the park (tens of metres wide) crosses in seconds, and so ramps give meaningful air from a flat push alone. Slopes and pumps go faster up to the speed cap.

coast_distance_8ms.why: Real wheels on smooth concrete roll 50 to 100 m from 8 m/s. Long enough to cross a park section and still carry into a ramp, short enough that a skater who stops pushing visibly slows down.

brake_distance_8ms.why: A foot drag from 8 m/s takes a real skater about 6 to 8 m. The game brakes a little harder so stopping for a trick spot feels controllable; below 3 m it feels like hitting a wall.

turn_radius_4ms.why: A real carve at walking-plus speed is 2 to 4 m; a kick turn is tighter. Tight low-speed turning lets the player line up rails and ramps in a small park.

turn_radius_8ms.why: A real carve at 8 m/s needs 8 to 12 m. THUG-style steering is much sharper; around 4 to 5 m lets the player thread a street line at speed without understeer.

turn_radius_12ms.why: Radius should grow with speed but stay well under a real skater's 15 m or more, so speed does not turn the game into a straight-line racer. It should be clearly wider than at 8 m/s (about 1.5x).

quarter_air_8ms.why: Height of the board above the coping of a 1.5 m mini ramp, from 8 m/s (a strong push plus a little downhill). Energy alone gives v^2/2g = 1.8 m at gravity 18, so a 1.5 m ramp can give at most about 0.3 m of air before rolling losses; this is the first, easy air a new player gets.

quarter_air_12ms.why: Height above the coping of a 1.5 m mini ramp from 12 m/s (a fast run-in). Pure energy gives 4.0 m minus the ramp height; the vert launch adds a little. Big, readable air that rewards speed without leaving the camera frame.

kicker_distance_8ms.why: Distance from the kicker lip to touchdown for the 2 m wide, 0.9 m high kicker at 8 m/s with no ollie. Enough to clear a small gap of 2 m with margin; real kickers at this speed give 2 to 3 m.

kicker_distance_12ms.why: Same kicker at 12 m/s. Distance should grow clearly with speed (about 1.5x, as flight time is fixed by the ramp angle and gravity) so faster run-ins clear bigger gaps, as in THUG's gap challenges.

landing_speed_retention.why: Horizontal speed just after a clean flat landing over just before it. A real clean landing loses almost nothing, so combos can chain; a few percent shows the impact without punishing a good landing.

halfpipe_pump_gain_per_cycle.why: Peak height above the coping gained per pass while pumping the first five passes of a 4 m halfpipe from 9 m/s. Real pumping adds 0.2 to 0.4 m per pass, but this is a design choice: Curtis wants to go super high after a few back-and-forths (8 m or more above the coping by the fifth pass). Pump gain grows with the square root of speed and the pump works up through the middle of the curve, so the first pass is already a real air (about 2 m over the coping; round 2 raised it from 1.1 m, which felt flat) and it builds about 2, 4.5, 6.5, 8, 9 m, levelling off near the speed cap. Under 1.2 the halfpipe never gets big; over 2.4 it is vert from the first minute.

loop_min_entry_speed.why: Lowest entry speed that makes it round the 4 m radius loop. Real physics needs sqrt(5*g*r), 14 m/s at g=9.8, but 19 m/s at the game's g=18. It must sit below the speed cap (22) with room to spare, yet above a push (about 12), so the loop needs a drop-in or a downhill run-in.

grind_speed_loss_per_m.why: Speed lost per metre on a flat rail at 8 m/s. Real metal-on-board friction costs 0.3 to 0.5 m/s per metre. The game wants long grinds to feel rewarding (a 10 m rail loses about 1.5 m/s) while still slowing a skater who sits on it too long.

roll_down_speed_bank3m.why: Speed at the toe of a 3 m high bank (about 31 degrees) from a standing roll-in, no pumping. Ideal energy gives sqrt(2*g*h) = 10.4 m/s at gravity 18, 7.7 m/s at real gravity. A small friction loss is right: a bank should feel like a free speed boost, but not a rocket.

push_accel_0_5.why: Mean acceleration from standing to 5 m/s by pushing. A real skater gets there in 2 to 3 kicks, about 1.5 to 2.5 m/s^2 (Exploratorium / longboard push studies). THUG gets you rolling in about a second; Skate 3 takes two or three visible kicks. 4.5 m/s^2 (about 1.1 s to 5 m/s) keeps it snappy but each kick still reads.

ollie_pop_latency_ms.why: Release of the ollie button to leaving the ground. THUG pops on release, on the next frame. Over two ticks (34 ms) starts to feel laggy on a 60 Hz game.

ollie_land_buffer_ms.why: An ollie tapped this long before touchdown still pops on landing (jump buffer). Platformer practice is about 100 to 120 ms (Celeste-style forgiveness, gamedev.net 'missed jump inputs'); it is what makes no-comply-style chains and stair-set hops feel responsive. Longer feels like the game is jumping on its own.

flip_rotations_per_s.why: Board flips per second (1 / flip_time). A real kickflip spins about 8 rev/s (frame counts of slow-mo kickflips, radratvideo); no game shows that, it reads as a blur. THUG kickflips take about 0.4 s, Skate 3 about 0.3 s. 2.4 rev/s (0.42 s) reads clearly and fits a tap ollie.

flip_catch_margin_tap_s.why: Air time of a tap ollie minus one flip: the time left to catch it. Positive means a tap kickflip on flat lands clean (THUG lets you); under 0.1 s it becomes a timing gamble; over 0.4 s flips are too easy to stack.

flip_prepop_buffer_ms.why: Flip pressed while still crouched for the ollie, this long before the pop, still flips after the pop. THUG players hit flip and jump almost together; a 0.1 to 0.2 s buffer catches 'too early' without firing stale presses.

spin_deg_full_ollie.why: Spin held through a full flat-ground ollie. THUG: a 360 is possible off flat with a full crouch, a 540 needs a kicker or a ramp. Skate 3 flat spins top out near 360. Under 340 a flat 360 is impossible; over 540 spins stop meaning anything.

spin_under_rotation_grace_deg.why: How far short of a half turn a spin can stop and still score it (150 counts as 180). THUG rounds generously; the landing heading tolerance below decides whether it is a clean landing.

land_clean_heading_max_deg.why: Largest angle between the board and the travel direction that still lands clean. Skate 3 is strict (about 20 to 30 deg before a powerslide-style sketchy landing); THUG is generous (about 45 to 60). We sit between, closer to THUG.

land_sketchy_heading_max_deg.why: Largest heading error that still rides away (sketchy). Past it the board is sideways to the travel and it is a bail, as in both games.

land_clean_tilt_max_deg.why: Board tilt off the landing surface that still lands clean (the auto-align usually fixes tilt for you, as in THUG). Over 40 deg on four wheels is a real-world slam.

sketchy_stagger_s.why: A sketchy landing (judged by Landing) staggers for about 0.4 s: the rider catches the board (Skate-3 foot-plant feel) with weak steering and a speed scrub, instead of a silent flat 20 percent loss.

sketchy_steer_ratio.why: Yaw turned in the first 0.25 s after touchdown with full stick, sketchy over clean: the stagger cuts the carve to about a third (tune.stagger_steer 0.35). 1.0 means a sketchy landing steers like a clean one.

sketchy_speed_keep.why: Speed 0.6 s after a sketchy touchdown over a clean landing's (same run, same full-stick carve): the stagger's scrub (tune.stagger_scrub, 12 percent) is the whole difference. The old flat 0.8 keep reads about 0.82 here (fails); over 0.93 makes sketchy free.

revert_pre_land_buffer_ms.why: Revert pressed this long before touchdown still reverts on landing. THUG players hit revert on the way down; a 0.1 to 0.2 s buffer matches platformer jump buffers. Measured to +-1 tick.

revert_post_land_window_ms.why: Revert pressed this long after touchdown still counts. It must at least match the 0.35 s combo land window so a revert can always extend the combo (THUG's rule), and stay short enough that a revert is a reaction to the landing.

manual_entry_window_ms.why: A manual flick (up, down) finished this long before touchdown still lands in a manual. THUG accepts the manual input on the way down; too short and players miss manual links off ramps.

manual_fall_nostick_s.why: A manual with no balance input falls after this long. THUG: hands off, the meter tips over in one to two seconds. Under 1.2 s is twitchy; over 3 s the balance is not a skill.

manual_hold_human_s.why: How long a steady player model (reacts 0.2 s late to the lean and its rate) holds a manual before the growing difficulty beats it. THUG manuals early in a combo last 10 to 20 s for a decent player and get harder the longer you hold.

grind_fall_nostick_s.why: Grind balance with no input (topples or bails after this long). Slightly more forgiving than the manual, as in THUG, where short rails need no balancing at all.

grind_hold_human_s.why: Same player model on a grind (speed held at 8 m/s). Long rail lines should be holdable but not free.

grind_snap_reach_m.why: Sideways distance from a rail at which pressing grind still snaps on. THUG is magnetic (about a body width either side); Skate 3 needs the trucks over the rail. 1 m is THUG-generous without grabbing rails you were not aiming at.

grind_press_buffer_ms.why: Grind pressed this long before the rail is in reach still grinds. Same 0.1 to 0.2 s buffer as the other presses; at 8 m/s that is 1 m of early press.

wallride_duration_s.why: Longest wallride. Real wallrides last a fraction of a second; THUG holds about 1 s, enough to wallie out or transfer. Longer turns walls into floors.

wall_slam_speed_ms.why: Square-on speed into a flat wall that slams. In Skate 3 even a moderate head-on hit is a bail; THUG almost never bails on walls. Above the push top speed (about 12) means a pushed run can bounce off a wall, but a downhill or ramp-fed run slams.

vert_air_14ms.why: Height above the coping of a 4 m quarter pipe (r 3.5) from 14 m/s, no pumping. Energy gives v^2/2g - 4 = 1.44 m at g 18; a little loss to rolling friction. Pro vert airs are 1.5 to 3.5 m over the coping (Danny Way's record 7.8 m off a mega quarter); the pump builds the rest.

vert_air_18ms.why: Same quarter from 18 m/s: energy gives 5.0 m. The air should follow energy closely (Skate-3-believable), with the vert launch neither adding nor stealing much.

wall_carve_speed_retention.why: Speed back on the flat over the speed at the toe after carving 45 degrees up a 2.5 m bowl wall and back down (about 1 s). Real wheels lose about 0.2 m/s per second (mu about 0.02, Kogelbauer et al. pumping study), about 0.97 here; a bowl carve must not feel like it brakes you.

slope_accel_15deg.why: Acceleration rolling down a 15 degree hill. Ideal g sin(15) = 4.66 at g 18; rolling friction takes about 0.6. Hills should feel like free speed, as in Skate 3's downhill runs.

dome_lap_speed_retention.why: Speed after one full hands-off lap round the practice DomeBowl (r 8 m, ring r 6.3 m, about 4.4 s, no pumping, no forward stick) over the speed at its start. Real wheels lose about 0.02 g in rolling resistance (Kogelbauer et al.), which at gravity 18 is about 0.36 m/s^2, so a 4.4 s lap at 9.5 m/s keeps about 0.92. Skate 3 bowls let you carve laps for many seconds before you must pump; THUG is more generous still. Round 3: roll_friction 0.6 gives 0.81 (draggy: a lap loses a fifth of its speed), 0.45 gives 0.89; held back until the bot lines are re-routed.

powerslide_decel_ms2.why: Mean deceleration over the first 0.5 s of a full-stick powerslide from 10 m/s. Skate 3 powerslides shed about half of 8 m/s in 0.7 s (about 6 m/s^2); a THUG-style slide must stop you faster than a foot brake (6 m/s^2 here) only slightly, so it is a tool to scrub speed into a spot, not a hard stop. Under 3.5 it is no better than the brake; over 9 it is a wall.

nollie_height_ratio.why: Tap nollie height over tap ollie height. A real nollie pops from the nose, a little lower and later (about 85 to 95 percent of the ollie, Apunts-style kinematics); THUG nollies match the ollie so nollie lines are just another stance. Under 0.8 nollie gaps would fail where ollie gaps pass; over 1.0 the nollie would be the better ollie.

grind_entry_speed_retention.why: Speed on the first tick of a grind over the speed just before the press, flat approach at 8 m/s. THUG snaps on with no loss; Skate 3 loses a few percent for the lock-on. Under 0.9 a grind entry feels like hitting a wall and kills combo flow.

manual_drift_1s.why: How much a 0.1 lean on the manual meter grows in one second with no stick. The meter is an unstable pendulum; THUG manuals roughly double their lean every half second. Under 2.5 the manual balances itself (no skill); over 5 a one-frame nudge is already a fall.

manual_recover_half_s.why: Time for a PD stick (proportional plus rate) to bring a half-tipped manual back under 0.1. The player must be able to catch a wobble in well under a second but not instantly: under 0.35 s the correction is a twitch, over 1 s a half-tipped manual is lost.

revert_speed_keep.why: Speed 12 ticks after touchdown with a revert on the landing tick over the same landing without it. A revert only switches stance (Skate 3 and THUG both keep speed through it); anything under 0.97 would make the revert a brake and break combo chains.

fakie_landing_retention.why: Horizontal speed 12 ticks after landing a 180 spin rolling backward (fakie) over the speed just before touchdown. Landing switch or fakie should cost no more than a forward landing (0.97 clean landing plus a little rolling friction); under 0.9 fakie lines feel punished.

big_air_clean_drop_m.why: Largest drop (2 m steps from 2 to 20) that an upright board still lands clean at 12 m/s. A mega ramp gap lands from 3 to 8 m (impact 12 to 18 m/s); Skate 3 slams on huge flat drops, THUG almost never bails on height. Upright landings slam once the speed square into the surface passes slam_impact (24 m/s, about a 16 m flat drop), so 14 m is the last clean step; transitions and banks that turn the fall into roll stay ridable. The band says: a mega ramp must never bail upright (8), and over 16 the height slam is missing.

big_air_landing_keep.why: Horizontal speed 12 ticks after an upright 8 m drop (mega ramp scale, 19 m/s impact) over the speed just before. The landing scrub is clamped (LAND_KEEP_MIN 0.95) so a huge hit costs at most about 5 percent of speed plus rolling friction; Skate 3 loses more on a flat slam, THUG nothing. Must not erase the speed of a big gap.

boneless_height_ratio.why: Boneless (up, up + ollie) height over a full-crouch ollie's. The front foot plants and the rider jumps with the board in hand, so it goes higher than any ollie: THUG2 bonelesses clear about a fifth more than a full ollie, the move for the extra height to a ledge. Under 1.1 it is not worth the plant; over 1.35 it replaces the kicker.

boneless_plant_ms.why: Release to pop of a boneless: the foot plant. Long enough to read on screen (a real boneless plant is a beat, about 0.1 to 0.2 s), short enough that the pop still lands where the player aimed it (THUG-snappy).

no_comply_height_ratio.why: No-comply (up + ollie) height over a tap ollie's. The back foot pops while the front foot steps off, a touch lower than an ollie (like the nollie), never higher.

wallplant_push_out_ms.why: Speed straight back out from the wall after a wallplant from 7 m/s. Skate 3 / THUG2 wallplants kick you back off the wall rather than up it: enough to clear the wall's foot and land rolling away, never a bounce faster than the approach.

wallplant_into_left_ms.why: Speed still going into the wall at the push (from 7 m/s): the planted foot kills most of it. Over 1 m/s the plant reads as sliding into the wall.

caveman_roll_speed_ms.why: Rolling speed after a caveman from a running jump on foot. The board is thrown down and caught at about running pace plus the jump's kick (a real caveman runs out at 4 to 6 m/s), so a caveman starts a line without pushing up to speed again.

acid_drop_energy_keep.why: Speed on the face after an acid drop over sqrt(v^2 + 2 g drop) at the press: dropping into a transition turns the fall into roll (Skate 3 physics, THUG2 generosity); a flat landing from the same air keeps under half of it.

grind_switch_speed_keep.why: Speed one tick after switching grinds mid-rail (grind + stick on the rail, THUG2) over the speed just before: the switch is a trick, not a brake, so a long rail can carry two or three grinds.

rail_transfer_speed_keep.why: Rail speed on the second rail of an ollie transfer (off the end of one rail onto the next in line) over the speed leaving the first: the hop keeps its run along the line (Skate 3 momentum), and THUG2 pays a Rail Transfer link for it.

grind_pop_charge_ratio.why: Height of an ollie off a rail after a full crouch (ollie held crouch_full s on the rail) over a tap's: pop timing matters as on the flat (1.9 / 1.0 m there), so a held pop clears a higher rail or a gap. (9.0 / 7.5)^2 = 1.44 at the defaults; the tap stays the old fixed 7.5 m/s so the levels' rail exits are unchanged.

lip_pop_flip_margin_s.why: Air time of a kickflip out of a lip trick (flip pressed in the stall: a pop of lip_pop up and out) less the flip's 0.42 s: room to catch it before the transition (THUG2 lip-to-air combos), not so much that the pop reads as a launch.
